nodes.description: A heterozygous 7.1-8.7 Mb deletion present in all cells. Reported cases share a common distal breakpoint at 16p12.2 and vary in the proximal breakpoint at 16p11.2, so the deleted gene set is not identical between patients - which is one reason gene-to-feature attribution has been hard to pin down. Deletions have been recurrent and de novo in the originally reported individuals.

nodes.description: Loss of one copy of dozens of genes simultaneously. That the phenotype follows from dosage across the interval is not in doubt; which genes carry which feature is. No gene in this interval has been shown to account for a feature of this syndrome on its own, and the gene-level candidates commonly cited for 16p come from studies of the smaller nested 16p11.2 CNVs rather than from this deletion. The node is therefore deliberately stated at the level the evidence supports.

nodes.description: The short arm of chromosome 16 is rich in segmental duplications. Complex low-copy repeats flank the 16p12.2-p11.2 interval, and misalignment between them during meiosis supports non-allelic homologous recombination, which excises the intervening segment. This is why the deletion recurs with reproducible breakpoints in unrelated individuals rather than occurring at random positions.
